title: Loong
synopsis: 2024 is the "Year of the Loong". Learn why Chinese state media have started referring to the Chinese dragon as the "loong" and the important place of this mythical animal in Chinese culture.

fullText.simplified:
龙

    2024年，中国农历龙年，官方媒体专门发布视频，纠正了“中国龙”的英文说法是“loong”而不是人们误用的“dragon”。这也说明了中国文化中的龙与西方语境中的龙有显著的差异。中国龙是农耕文明的产物，主要负责保佑一方风调雨顺，承载着勇敢奋进、活力无穷、吉祥如意等美好寓意。
    龙，是中国古代神话中的动物。相传龙能飞行，擅变化，会呼风唤雨等，与凤凰、麒麟等并列为祥瑞。在汉文化中，龙有着重要的地位和影响。
    中国的传统建筑中有龙。以有600多年历史的故宫为例，龙不仅出现在宫殿里，还出现在服饰、家具、钟表、器皿等各类物品上。仅太和殿，上上下下就有近13000条“龙”。
    中国的传统民俗中有龙，舞龙最为流行。每到节日，人们都会舞龙，比如春节、端午节等。以舞龙的方式来祈求平安和丰收是中国各地汉族的一种民俗文化。
    中国的传统节日中有龙。农历二月二是中国的“龙抬头节”。此时大地逐渐转暖，一年的农事活动将要开始。民俗认为二月二这一天人们的食物都是龙身上之物，如：面条是龙须、烙饼是龙鳞、饺子是龙耳等等。于是人们在二月二会吃面条、烙饼，因为食龙须和龙鳞对龙伤害不大；不能吃米饭，因为米饭是龙子，一顿米饭要伤害很多龙。
    汉语中也有很多与龙相关的成语。“人中龙凤”指的是人群中的佼佼者；“望子成龙”说的是希望孩子能成为“龙”，可以非常优秀；“生龙活虎”说的是人非常有活力，像龙和虎一样活泼灵敏；“车水马龙”被用来形容热闹繁荣的景象；“龙马精神”说的是人努力向上的精神和样子。春节时，人们常常会祝福别人“龙马精神”。
    总而言之，“龙”对中国人来说非常重要，它对人们的生活和文化有着重要和深远的影响。
fullText.traditional:
龍

    2024年，中國農曆龍年，官方媒體專門發布視頻，糾正了“中國龍”的英文說法是“loong”而不是人們誤用的“dragon”。這也說明了中國文化中的龍與西方語境中的龍有顯著的差異。中國龍是農耕文明的產物，主要負責保佑一方風調雨順，承載著勇敢奮進、活力無窮、吉祥如意等美好寓意。
    龍，是中國古代神話中的動物。相傳龍能飛行，擅變化，會呼風喚雨等，與鳳凰、麒麟等並列為祥瑞。在漢文化中，龍有著重要的地位和影響。
    中國的傳統建築中有龍。以有600多年歷史的故宮為例，龍不僅出現在宮殿裡，還出現在服飾、家具、鐘錶、器皿等各類物品上。僅太和殿，上上下下就有近13000條“龍”。
    中國的傳統民俗中有龍，舞龍最為流行。每到節日，人們都會舞龍，比如春節、端午節等。以舞龍的方式來祈求平安和豐收是中國各地漢族的一種民俗文化。
    中國的傳統節日中有龍。農曆二月二是中國的“龍抬頭節”。此時大地逐漸轉暖，一年的農事活動將要開始。民俗認為二月二這一天人們的食物都是龍身上之物，如：麵條是龍鬚、烙餅是龍鱗、餃子是龍耳等等。於是人們在二月二會吃麵條、烙餅，因為食龍鬚和龍鱗對龍傷害不大；不能吃米飯，因為米飯是龍子，一頓米飯要傷害很多龍。
    漢語中也有很多與龍相關的成語。“人中龍鳳”指的是人群中的佼佼者；“望子成龍”說的是希望孩子能成為“龍”，可以非常優秀；“生龍活虎”說的是人非常有活力，像龍和虎一樣活潑靈敏；“車水馬龍”被用來形容熱鬧繁榮的景象；“龍馬精神”說的是人努力向上的精神和樣子。春節時，人們常常會祝福別人“龍馬精神”。
    總而言之，“龍”對中國人來說非常重要，它對人們的生活和文化有著重要和深遠的影響。

sentence_translations: Loong
2024 is the Year of the Loong according to the Chinese lunar calendar.
Official media released a video to clarify that the correct English term for “中国龙” is “loong” instead of the incorrectly used “dragon”.
This also indicates that there are significant differences between the loong of Chinese culture and the dragon in Western contexts.
The Chinese loong is a product of agricultural civilization.
It is mainly responsible for blessing the local area with favorable weather.
It embodies the positive connotations of courage and progress, boundless energy, and good fortune.
The loong is an animal from ancient Chinese mythology.
According to legend, the loong can fly, is adept at transformation, and can summon wind and rain.
It is regarded alongside the fenghuang [Chinese phoenix] and the qilin [Chinese unicorn] as an auspicious symbol.
In Han Chinese culture, the loong holds an important position and influence.
The loong is prevalent in traditional Chinese architecture.
Taking the Forbidden City, which has a history of over 600 years, as an example, ..
.. loongs not only appear in the palaces but also on clothing, furniture, clocks, utensils, and various other items.
There are nearly 13,000 “loongs” throughout the Hall of Supreme Harmony alone.
The loong is present in traditional Chinese folk customs, with the loong dance being the most popular.
During festivals, people perform loong dances, such as during the Spring Festival and the Dragon Boat Festival.
Praying for peace and a bountiful harvest through loong dances is a folk culture of the Han people across various regions of China.
The loong is present in traditional Chinese festivals.
The second day of the second lunar month is China’s “Longtaitou Festival”.
During this time, the land gradually warms up, and the year’s farming activities are about to begin.
According to folklore, everything that people eat on the second day of the second lunar month is from the body of the loong.
For example, noodles are the beard of the loong, laobing are the scales of the loong, jiaozi are the ears of the loong, and so on.
So, people will eat noodles and laobing on the second day of the second month ..
.. because eating the beard of the loong and the scales of the loong does not harm the loong much.
It is not allowed to eat rice because rice is the offspring of the loong, and eating a meal of rice would harm many loongs.
There are also many idioms related to the loong in Chinese.
“A loong and fenghuang among people” refers to outstanding individuals in a group.
“Hoping one’s children can become a loong” means hoping they can become outstanding.
“Lively loong and animated tiger” describes an energetic person, someone lively and agile like the loong and tiger.
“Carriages like a stream and horses like a loong” is used to describe a bustling and flourishing scene.
“The spirit of the loong and horse” refers to the spirit and appearance of someone who strives to improve and progress.
During the Spring Festival, people often wish others “the spirit of the loong and horse.”
In summary, the “loong” is very important to Chinese people.
It has a significant and profound impact on people’s lives and culture.
